children: fell 1.54% premarket after reporting third-quarter earnings of $1.19 per diluted share on revenue of $8.0 billion, compared to $1.29 and $8.319 billion Wall Street expected. Net earnings fell to $284 million from $591 million. New orders dropped 9% to 20,879 homes and deliveries 3% to 20,840. CEO Stuart Miller said the results "were below expectations," citing a deteriorating environment and a 30-year mortgage rate at about 6.8% at quarter end.
Gross margin on home sales fell to 15.8% from 17.5%, with SG&A rising to 9.2% of home sales revenue from 8.2%, leaving a net margin of 6.6%. Average sales price dropped to $372,000 from $383,000.

Homebuilding cash fell to $1.15 billion from $3.44 billion at November 30, while inventory owned rose to $11.5 billion from $9.9 billion. Net homebuilding debt to total capital went to 12.7% from 2.8%. Lennar repurchased 3 million shares for $256 million at an average of $85.49 and redeemed $400 million of senior notes.

Looking forward, full-year deliveries are now guided to 80,000 to 81,000 homes, down from 82,000 to 83,000. For the fourth quarter, new orders are guided to 19,500 to 20,500 homes with an average sales price of $370,000 to $380,000.

title: Lennar Misses and Cuts Full-Year Delivery Guidance
